# WHY THIS DATASET MATTERS (for OpenRocket Plus transonic base drag validation)
# This is a PRIMARY
# drag on a cylindrical-afterbody body of revolution. It contains all three
# conditions needed to isolate the physical sting-free base drag:
#   (i)   Config A  -- finless free-flight (NO sting
#   (ii)  Config B  -- same body with SIMULATED REAR-SUPPORT STING
#   (iii) Config C  -- fin-stabilized free-flight (reference 3
# Hart's Figure 6 directly shows that a sting reduces base suction by 40%
# at subsonic speeds but has NO measurable effect at M > 1.15
# exactly the contamination that was present in the Compton NASA TN D-4821
# wind-tunnel data (M 0.95-1.20) that the original authors themselves rejected.
# Hart Configuration A is therefore a defensible
# transonic base-drag source directly comparable to OpenRocket Plus's
# polynomial transonic base-drag peak.
# MODEL GEOMETRY
#   Shape:          ogive-cylinder
#   Nose:           3.5-caliber ogival nose joined to cylinder
#   Base:           FLAT
#   Reference area: body cross-sectional (frontal) area
#   Stability:      internal nose-ballasting (Config A/D) or nose sting (F)
#                   to keep center-of-gravity forward
#   Support:        FREE-FLIGHT AFTER BOOSTER SEPARATION (no sting contamination)
#   Tracking:       Doppler velocimeter + SCR-584 theodolite radar
#   Atmosphere:     radiosonde balloon released immediately after each flight
#   Re_L:           15e6 to 45e6 (increasing with M per figure 5)
#   Drag probable error: < 4% (flight-to-flight repeatability on previously
#                         tested Config E used to estimate)
#   Base-pressure probable error: +-0.030 at M=0.8
#   Mach number probable error:   +-0.01
